The size, slope, alignment, materials of construction of a building sewer, and the methods to be used in construction shall all conform to the requirements of the building and plumbing codes and other applicable rules and regulations of the city and county. In the absence of code provisions or in amplification thereof, the materials and procedures set forth in appropriate specifications of the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) and Water Pollution Control Federation (WPCF) Manual of Practice No. 9 shall apply. Additionally, the following materials and methods shall apply to building sewers within the city's supervision:
(1) The building sewer shall be cast iron soil pipe, ASTM Specification A74, latest revision, or equal; ductile iron pipe, American National Standards Institute (ANSI) Specification A21.51, latest revision, or equal; ASTM C200 extra strength clay pipe; or polyvinyl chloride (PVC) sewer pipe Schedule 40, ASTM Specification D3034, latest revision. All joints shall be tight and waterproof. Any part of the building sewer that is located within ten (10) feet of a water service pipe shall be constructed of cast iron soil pipe; ductile iron pipe with bolted mechanical joints may be required by the superintendent where the sewer is exposed to damage by tree roots. If installed in filled or unstable ground, the building sewer shall be of cast iron soil pipe, except that plastic pipe may be acceptable if laid on a suitable concrete bed or cradle as approved by the superintendent.
(2) The size and slope of the building sewer shall be subject to the approval of the superintendent, but in no event shall the diameter be less than four (4) inches. The slope of such four-inch pipe shall not be less than one-eighth inch per foot. Furthermore, the appropriate requirements of the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OSHA) shall be followed.
(3) The depth shall be sufficient to afford protection from frost, and the building sewer shall be laid at uniform grade and with straight alignment insofar as possible. Changes in direction shall be made only with properly curved pipe and fittings. Building sewers shall not be placed in the same trench with water service lines. A cleanout plug shall be provided at the building and at each ninety (90) degree turn outside the building. Ninety (90) degree turns shall be made by using two (2) one-eighth bends or a long sweep ell.
(4) An excavation required for the installation of a building sewer shall be open trench work unless otherwise approved by the superintendent. Pipe laying and backfill shall be performed in accordance with ASTM Specification C12, latest revision, except that no backfill shall be placed until the work has been inspected and approved.
(5) All joints and connections shall be made gastight and watertight.
a. Push-on joints for cast iron soil pipe shall have neoprene gaskets in accordance with the requirements of ASTM C-564.
b. Push-on joints for ductile iron pipe shall also have neoprene gaskets and be installed according to the manufacturer's recommendations.
c. Vitrified clay pipe joints shall conform to ASTM C425 using material having resilient properties; Type III, O ring gasket. Gaskets shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
d. PVC pipe joint material shall be of the bell and spigot type, sealed with a rubber O ring gasket, having a composition and texture which is resistant to the common ingredients of sewage, industrial wastes (including oils), and ground water, and which will endure permanently under the conditions likely to be imposed by this use. Installation of gasket shall be done in accordance with the pipe manufacturer's instructions using all the necessary materials, lubricants, and equipment recommended by the manufacturer.
e. Other jointing materials may be used only when approved by the city. Connection of pipe of different materials shall be made by using appropriate adaptors approved by the city.
(6) The connection of the building sewer into the public sewer shall be made at the Y branch, if such a branch is available at a suitable location. If the public sewer is twelve (12) inches in diameter or less, and no properly located Y branch is available, the city shall, at the owner's expense, cut a neat hole into the public sewer, with entry in the downstream direction at an angle of about forty-five (45) degrees, and install a 45-degree elbow with the spigot end cut so as not to extend past the inner surface of the public sewer. The invert of the building sewer at the point of connection shall be at an elevation of at least one-tenth foot above the invert of the public sewer. A neat smooth joint shall be made, and the connection made secure and watertight by encasement in concrete. Special fittings may be used for the connection only when approved by the city.

(1) Any gasoline, benzene, naphtha, fuel oil or other flammable or explosive liquid, solid or gas.
(2) Any waters containing toxic or poisonous solids, liquids or gases in sufficient quantity, either singly or by interaction with other wastes, to damage or interfere with any waste treatment process, constitute a hazard to humans or animals, create a public nuisance or create any hazard in the receiving waters of the wastewater treatment plant.

511:
The following described substances, materials, waters or waste shall be limited in discharges to municipal systems to concentrations or quantities which will not harm either the sewers, wastewater treatment process or equipment, will not have an adverse effect on the receiving stream, or will not otherwise endanger lives, limb or public property, or constitute a nuisance. The limitations or restrictions on materials or characteristics of waste or wastewater discharged to the sanitary sewer which shall not be violated without approval of the city are as follows:
(1) Wastewater having a temperature higher than one hundred fifty (150) degrees Fahrenheit (sixty-five (65) degrees Celsius) or wastewater which will elevate the temperature of the influent to the publicly-owned treatment works (POTW) to one hundred four (104) degrees Fahrenheit (forty (40) degrees Celsius) or higher.
(2) Wastewater containing more than twenty-five (25) milligrams per liter of petroleum oil, nonbiodegradable cutting oils or product of mineral oil origin.

(4) Any garbage that has not been properly shredded. 543:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Air gap separation means the unobstructed vertical distance through the free atmosphere between the lowest opening from any pipe or faucet supplying pure water to a tank, plumbing fixture or other device and the rim of the receptacle.
Auxiliary water system means any water system on or available to the premises other than the water works, which may include, but is not limited to, other purveyors water works, wells, lakes, streams, process fluids or used water. Auxiliary water system maybe polluted, contaminated, objectionable or constitute a system over which the water purveyor has no control.
Backflow means a reverse flow of contaminants, pollution, process fluids, used water, untreated water, chemicals, gases, nonpotable water into any part of a water system.
Backflow prevention means a program designed to prevent backflow into the potable water systems and to discover, to eliminate, and to prevent all uncontrolled cross-connections, existing or potential.
Backflow prevention device means a device designed to prevent reverse flow in a water system. The term "backflow prevention" will be used in reference to an approved or listed device by one of the recognized testing agencies.
Backpressure means an increase in pressure in a consumer's water system, or a branch of the system, above that at the service-connection. It is generally caused by pumps, thermal expansion, or reasons other than a reduction or loss of the incoming pressure. Backpressure is generally more evident in a closed water system.
Backsiphonage means a reverse flow in a water system caused by a negative pressure in the incoming pipe, when the point of use is at atmospheric pressure. Backsiphonage is generally more evident in an open water system.
Closed water system means one with a checking device installed in the service pipe. A check valve, backflow preventer, or pressure reducing valve would create a closed system.
Consumer means the owner or person in control of any premises supplied by or in any manner connected to a waterworks.
Consumer's water system means all potable water piping, valves, fittings and appurtenances on the premises side of the service-connection. It is the secondary component of a public water system.
Consumer's water system means any water system located on the consumer's premises supplied by or in any manner connected to a waterworks.
Containment means any substance that, if introduced into the potable water system, could create a health hazard.
Containment backflow prevention means the installation of a backflow preventer at the service-connection to premises to protect the water main primarily (the second line of defense).
Contamination means any introduction into pure water of microorganisms, wastes, wastewater, undesirable chemicals, or gases.
Cross-connection means a physical connection or arrangement between two otherwise separate piping systems, one of which contains potable water, the other nonpotable fluid, or water of unknown quality, where there could be backflow into the potable system unless it is protected by an appropriate backflow prevention device.
Cross-connection means any connection or structural arrangement, direct or indirect, to the waterworks whereby backflow can occur.
Cross-connection control (isolation) means the installation of a backflow preventer at each cross-connection on a premises for protection at the point of use (the first line of defense).
Cross-connection inspector means a person qualified and authorized to make internal inspections for uncontrolled plumbing cross-connections, to prescribe means for controlling same, and who has proved his competency to the applicable regulatory agency(ies).
Degree of hazard is derived from an evaluation of the potential risk to health and the adverse effect upon the waterworks.
Double detector check backflow preventer (DDC-BFP) means a backflow prevention device designed to serve also as a detector check on fire protection systems where pollutants are involved. It includes a line-sized approved double check valve backflow preventer with a metered bypass, into which has been incorporated a three-quarter inch approved double check valve backflow preventer.
Double gate-double check valve assembly (DCV-BFP) means an approved assembly composed of two single, independently acting check valves including tightly closing shutoff valves located at each end of the assembly and petcocks and test gauges for testing the water tightness of each check valve.
Dual check backflow preventer (DuC-BFP) means a small backflow prevention device designed especially for containing water systems to residences, mobile homes, etc., as the second line of defense, and for isolating residential lawn sprinkler systems, etc., where pollutants are involved.
Hazard, degree of, means an impurity that varies in severity from mildly toxic to lethal.
Health hazard means any condition, device, or practice in a waterworks or its operation that creates, or may create, a danger to the health and well-being of the water consumer.
Nonpressure type cross-connection means a low-inlet installation where a potable water pipe is connected or extended below the overflow rim of a receptacle, or an environment, that contains a nonpotable fluid, and is at atmospheric pressure.
Open water system means one with no checking device installed in the service pipe. Water from the consumer's system is free to backflow into the main, for whatever reason.
Pollutant means any substance that, if introduced into the potable water system, could be objectionable but could not create a health hazard.
Pollution means the presence of any foreign substance (chemical, physical, radiological, or biological) in water that tends to degrade its quality so as to constitute an unnecessary risk or impair the usefulness of the water.
Pollution hazard means a condition through which an aesthetically objectionable or degrading material may enter the waterworks or a consumer's water system.
Pressure type cross-connection means an installation where a potable water pipe is connected to a closed vessel, or a piping system, that contains a nonpotable fluid, and is above atmospheric pressure.
Process fluids means any fluid or solution that may be chemically, biologically, or otherwise contaminated or polluted which would constitute a health, pollutional, or system hazard introduced into the waterworks. This includes, but not limited to:
(1) Polluted or contaminated waters;
(2) Process waters;
(3) Used waters originating from the waterworks which may have deteriorates in sanitary quality;
(4) Cooling waters;
(5) Contaminated natural waters taken from wells, lakes, streams, or irrigation systems;
(6) Chemicals in solution or suspension; and
(7) Oils, gases, acids, alkalis, and other liquid and gaseous fluids used in industrial or other processes, or for fire fighting purposes.
Public water supply means a system operated as a public utility that supplies potable water to the service connection of the consumer's water system. It is the primary component of a public water system.
Reduced pressure detector check backflow preventer (RPDC-BFP) means a backflow prevention device designed to serve also as a detector check on fire protection systems where contaminants are involved. It includes a line-size approved reduced pressure zone backflow preventer with a metered bypass, into which has been incorporated a three-quarter-inch approved reduced pressure zone backflow preventer.
Reduced pressure zone backflow preventer (RPZ-BFP) means a backpressure and backsiphonage-type backflow prevention device designed to operate under continuous pressure, including backpressure, where contaminants are involved.
Service connection means the point of delivery of water to premises, including the meter. It is the end of the water purveyor's jurisdiction and the beginning of the plumbing official's jurisdiction.
Vacuum breaker, hose type (HVB) means a backsiphonage prevention device designed for hose connections only, but not for continuous pressure, static or flowing.
Vacuum relief valve means a device designed to limit the degree of vacuum in a vessel or pipe, but not for cross-connection control.
(Ord. No. 2020-07-01, § 2, 8-20-2020)
544:
A program is hereby established as the city cross-connection control program, which shall be administered by the Director of Public Works or his duly appointed representative.
(Ord. No. 2020-07-01, § 2, 8-20-2020)
545:
(a) Program purpose.
(1) To protect the public water supply system of the city from the possibility of contamination or pollution by isolating within its customers internal distribution systems such contaminants or pollutants which could backflow or be back siphoned into the city's water system.
(2) To eliminate or control the existing cross-connection, actual or potential, at each water outlet from the consumer's service line.
(3) To provide for the maintenance of a continuing program of cross-connections control which will systematically and efficiently prevent the contamination or pollution of the potable water system.
(b) Right of entry. The city as purveyor of water shall have the right of entry of any building or premise where cross-connections or possible contamination is evident or suspected for the course of protection of the public water system and the health and safety of its consumers the referral of said access for said purpose shall be deemed evidence of the presence of a cross-connection and subsequently in violation of these program requirements.
(c) Violations.
(1) Low degree hazard. Violators of these program requirements shall be notified and allowed five days to provide subsequent changes to cease the said violations.
(2) All but low degree hazards shall be notified within 24 hours and required to immediately cease or cause to cease said violation.
(3) If violations are not remedied to the satisfaction of the director of public works within the time period allowed, the water service to such premises shall be ceased and the water meter removed. Reestablishment of service shall be at the consumer's expense.
(Ord. No. 2020-07-01, § 2, 8-20-2020)
546:
(a) All new services to the city public water system shall meet the program requirements at the time of occupancy or when water usage begins.
(b) Any structures or water services that are added to, altered or remodeled shall meet the requirements of the program with the exceptions as follows: Single-family and double-family structures unless they have a private non-regulated water source on the property, an irrigation system or other potentially hazardous process or otherwise deemed necessary that a safety hazard exists.
(c) Existing services not included in subsection (a) or (b) of this section will be surveyed and prioritized according to degree of hazard (low, moderate, high) and required to meet this cross-connection control program on that basis.
(d) Any backflow prevention device must be installed adjacent to and down stream of the metering point or point of receiving service. This will be the device which separates the city owned and maintained lines from the users lines, exceptions may be granted by the director of public works to locate the device inside a structure if:
(1) The service line is 50 feet or less;
(2) An acceptable location is provided with access from the outside; and
(3) The service line is not laid in any type of contamination as defined by the EPD or the city.
All three conditions must exist for an exception to be granted.
(e) Any user with contaminants on their property, or used in any process by the user, must use the reduced pressure zone backflow preventer for cross-connection control requirements.
(f) All other domestic users (except in subsection (e) of this section) must use the double check valve backflow preventer for cross-connection control requirements.
(g) Fire protection systems shall use detector devices. Class 1, 2 and 3 shall use double detector check backflow preventers and any system that has contaminants used in them shall use reduced pressure zone detector backflow preventers for cross-connection control requirements. Fire protection systems shall be protected from the public water as follows:
(1) Class 1, 2 and 3 systems shall be protected from the public mains by installing an approved double detector check backflow preventer.
(2) Class 4 and 5 sprinkler systems, and hazardous standpipe systems, shall be protected by an approved (RPZ) reduced pressure zone detector check backflow preventer.
(3) Class 6 sprinkler systems, and standpipe systems of similar degree of potential hazard, shall be protected by procedures determined after a survey of the premises.
(4) Combined sprinkler and standpipe systems shall be protected from the public mains by procedures applicable to the component that requires the higher degree of protection as determined by the director of public works.
(h) Irrigation services of one inch and less may use a dual check valve backflow preventer, in lieu of a reduced pressure zone backflow preventer, if no chemicals are used at any time in the irrigation system if approved by the director of public works.
(i) Irrigation systems larger than one inch may use a double check valve backflow preventer in lieu of a reduced pressure zone backflow preventer, if no chemicals are used at any time in the irrigation system if approved by the director of public works.
(j) Irrigation systems of any size that use any type of chemicals (permanent or temporary) shall use a reduced pressure zone backflow preventer for cross-connection control.
(k) Irrigation systems that use alternate sources of water shall use reduced pressure zone backflow preventers on the city supply line for cross-connection control requirements irregardless whether the alternate source and the city supply are interconnected.
(l) Every service on the system shall be reviewed for program requirements in order of potential degree of hazard as prioritized by the director of public works or his designee.
(m) Any person who performs tests, repairs or maintains a backflow prevention device shall be certified under guidelines acceptable to the director of public works or his designee.
(n) Any person who installs a backflow preventer must be a Georgia licensed plumber, hold a certificate of competency for fire suppression systems from the State of Georgia, or be a certified backflow prevention device specialist.
(o) Any gauge or instrument used in the testing of backflow preventers shall be calibrated once every two years and a record of that calibration shall be submitted to the director of public works.
(Ord. No. 2020-07-01, § 2, 8-20-2020)
547:
(a) New water service.
(1) All new water services shall have installed a backflow prevention device acceptable to these regulations and to the director of public works.
(2) Residential services shall have a backflow prevention device installed prior to the meter/service installation.
(3) All water services shall have a backflow prevention device designed and installed by the owner at his expense with the approval of the director of public works or his designee.
(4) Water service shall not commence until the requirements of this cross-connection program have been complied with.
(5) Private wells shall not be connected to a service with a backflow prevention device installed.
(b) Existing service being added to, altered or remodeled.
(1) The city shall reserve the option of requiring a backflow prevention device to be added to residential services.
(2) Residential services. Residential services (single-family and two-family dwellings) are not included unless the following:
a. The director of public works deems it necessary to protect the water system from a known or suspected hazard.
b. An irrigation system or a private water source exists on the property.
c. Private wells are not allowed to be interconnected with the service from the city under any circumstances. All property that has a private well shall have a reduced pressure zone principal backflow prevention device installed on the city supply line to the property.

(c) The owner shall be responsible for the payment of all fees for permits, annual or semi-annual device testing, retesting in the case that the device fails to operate correctly, and second re-inspections for noncompliance with the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2020-07-01, § 2, 8-20-2020)
548:
(a) All backflow devices shall be tested and inspected at least annually.
(b) Testing must be performed by a licensed backflow tester approved by the State of Georgia.
(c) Any backflow preventer which fails during a periodic test will be repaired or replaced at owner's expense. Based on the experiences of other counties and municipalities, including, but not limited to, Austin, Texas, and Garden Grove, California, which experiences are found to be relevant to the problem faced by the City of Grovetown, Georgia; and based on the documentary evidence and oral testimony presented by a law enforcement professional and an expert in economic development, both of whom are familiar with conditions resulting in other localities, at the city council's hearing on May 14 and June 14, 2004; and based on the evidence and testimony of persons who appeared before members of the city council on other occasions including the public hearing conducted on May 14 and June 14, 2004, and on documentary evidence submitted to the city council, the city council takes note of the well-known and self-evident conditions and secondary effects attendant to the commercial exploitation of human sexuality, which do not vary greatly among the various communities within our country.
It is the finding of the city council that public nudity (either partial or total) under certain circumstances, particularly circumstances related to the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages in establishments offering live nude entertainment or adult entertainment, (whether such alcoholic beverages are sold on the premises or not) begets criminal behavior and tends to create undesirable community conditions. In the same manner, establishments offering cinematographic or video graphic adult entertainment have the same deleterious effects on the community.
Among the acts of criminal behavior found to be associated with the commercial combination of live nudity and alcohol, live commercial nudity in general, and cinematographic or video graphic adult entertainment are disorderly conduct, prostitution, public solicitation, public indecency, drug use and drug trafficking. Among the undesirable community conditions identified in other communities with the commercial combination of live nudity and alcohol, commercial nudity in general, and cinematographic or video graphic adult entertainment are depression of property values and acceleration of community blight in the surrounding neighborhood, increase allocation of and expenditure for law enforcement personnel to preserve law and order, and increased burden on the judicial system as a consequence of the criminal behavior hereinabove described. The city council finds it is reasonable to believe that some or all of these undesirable community conditions will result in the city, as well.
Furthermore, it is the finding of the city council that other forms of adult entertainment, including, but not limited to, adult book stores, adult novelty shops, adult video stores, peep shows, adult theaters, and massage parlors have an adverse effect upon the quality of life surrounding communities.
The city council finds that the negative secondary effects of adult entertainment establishments upon the city are similar whether the adult entertainment establishment features live nude dancing or sells video tapes depicting sexual activities.
The city council therefore finds it is in the best interests of the health, welfare, safety and morals of the community and the preservation of its businesses, neighborhoods, and of churches, schools, residential areas, public parks and children's day care facilities to prevent or reduce the adverse impacts of adult entertainment establishments. Therefore, the city council finds that licensing and regulations promote public welfare by furthering legitimate public and governmental interests, including, but not limited to, reducing criminal activity and protecting against or eliminating undesirable community conditions and further finds that such will not infringe upon the protected Constitutional rights of freedom of speech or expression. To that end, this article is hereby adopted.

Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file an application with the licensing and revenue manager on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. Applications for renewal must be filed before November 30 of each year. Any renewal application received after November 30 shall pay, in addition to said annual regulatory fee, a late charge of twenty (20) percent. If a license renewal application is received after January 1, such application shall be treated as an initial application and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules and regulations for the granting of licenses as if no previous license has been held. If a license application is received after January 1, investigative and administrative costs as hereinafter set forth in this article will be assessed. All licenses granted hereunder shall be for the calendar year and the full annual regulatory fee must be paid for a license renewal application. Any person renewing any license issued hereunder who shall pay the annual regulatory fee, or any portion thereof, after January 1, shall, in addition to said regulatory fee and late charges, pay simple interest on the delinquent balance at the annual rate then charged by the Internal Revenue Service of the United States on unpaid federal income taxes.
(Code 2012, § 10-88; Ord. No. 158, § 3, 7-12-2004)
